title: Gaps, Imbalances & Price Delivery
hook: Clear the Price Delivery Lab, pass the Knowledge Check and save your Check-In to unlock Section 9.

game.title: Price Delivery Lab ⚡
game.tagline: Nine experiments. See the trip, not just the destination.
game.doneBadge: Price Delivery Lab: all 9 levels cleared
game.doneLine: You saw slow and displaced delivery, found imbalance and FVGs, refused to assume a fill, chose the gap that mattered, and kept structure first and the entry model clean.

levels.body: How did price travel? Go fast.

items.why: Small candles with lots of overlap.
Big one-way candles, little overlap.
Fast and one-sided, down.
A grind lower with overlap.
Mostly big candles in one direction.
Back-and-forth with lots of overlap.

levels.passText: Slow or displaced: you see the trip.
levels.name: Slow or displaced?

debrief.saw: Some moves crawled with overlap. Some traveled fast with big one-way candles.
debrief.know: Delivery can be described as overlapping or displaced.
debrief.unknown: Where any of these moves goes next.

steps.text: Three highlighted areas. One of them shows price moving with little two-sided trading.

pick.hint: Look for big candles with almost no overlap.

notes.A: Lots of overlap there. Both sides traded.
notes.C: Small candles going sideways. Plenty of overlap.

pick.why: The fast leg: big candles, little overlap.

levels.name: Find the imbalance
levels.goal: Where did both sides barely trade?

debrief.saw: A slow start, a fast leg up, and a sideways finish.
debrief.know: The fast leg looks imbalanced: big candles with little overlap.
debrief.unknown: Whether price ever comes back to it.

levels.body: Three candles. Gap between candle 1 and candle 3? Build a streak.

items.why: Candle 3’s low stayed above candle 1’s high.
Candle 3 traded back into candle 1’s range.
Bearish: candle 3’s high stayed below candle 1’s low.
Candle 3’s wick reached all the way back.
Small overlapping candles.
A clean gap between candle 1’s high and candle 3’s low.
Bearish FVG.
Candle 3’s low dipped back below candle 1’s high.

levels.passText: Fast eyes. Now the real question: does it matter?
levels.name: FVG or no FVG?
levels.goal: Candle 1 and candle 3. Is there a gap?

debrief.know: An FVG needs a gap between candle 1 and candle 3. Overlap means no FVG.
debrief.unknown: Whether any of these gaps would matter on a real chart.

items.text: Does price have to fill this FVG?
items.why: No gap has to fill.

items.text: Does price have to return to this imbalance at all?
items.why: It may. It may not.

items.text: Price came back and filled it. Does that prove every FVG must fill?
items.why: One fill proves one fill. Nothing more.

debrief.saw: A bullish FVG, then price came back and filled it.
debrief.know: This FVG filled. That’s one outcome.
debrief.unknown: Whether the next FVG fills. Each one is its own story.

steps.text: Price broke the prior low with displacement and is pulling back up.

pick.prompt: Which FVG is most relevant right now?
pick.hint: Which one formed in the move that broke the prior low?

notes.A: A formed in old messy price and was traded through.
notes.C: C is old and already traded through.

pick.why: B: formed in the break, near where price is now.

debrief.saw: Three bearish FVGs: one old, one in messy price, one in the move that broke the prior low.
debrief.know: B formed in the break and price is pulling back toward it. Relevant context.
debrief.unknown: Whether price reacts there, and whether an entry model ever forms.

steps.text: A bearish FVG just appeared. Before you look at it: structure first.

options.label: Bullish: higher highs and higher lows
Bearish, there’s a bearish FVG
options.feedback: An FVG isn’t structure. Read the swings.

asks.prompt: Does the bearish FVG change that structure?

options.label: No. The supporting HL is intact
options.why: Delivery inside the structure. Structure unchanged.

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Which level would need to break?

lens.context: Bearish displacement in the pullback, leaving a bearish FVG.
lens.execution: Entry model: not present / not being evaluated yet

levels.name: Structure first
levels.goal: Read the swings before the boxes.

debrief.saw: A bullish structure with a sharp pullback that left a bearish FVG.
debrief.know: The structure is still bullish. The FVG describes the pullback’s delivery.
debrief.unknown: Whether the pullback keeps going or the structure holds.

items.why: Market literacy.
Part of the Dayli ICC sequence.
A description of delivery.
Not a step. Never required.
Part of the Dayli ICC sequence.
Market literacy.

levels.prompt: Concept, or a step in the Dayli ICC entry sequence?
levels.name: Concept or entry?
levels.goal: Sort the language from the method.

debrief.saw: A mix of delivery concepts and entry-sequence steps.
debrief.know: FVGs, fills, displacement and imbalance are concepts. Correction and retest are entry steps.
debrief.unknown: Nothing here. This one is a rule: concepts don’t become steps.

items.text:
✓ Valid Dayli ICC sequence · ✗ No FVG
Automatically invalid?
items.why: No FVG is required. The setup stands on its own.

items.text:
✓ Valid Dayli ICC sequence · ✗ FVG not filled yet
Wait for the fill first?
items.why: A fill is never a requirement.
The FVG doesn’t replace the sequence.

levels.name: Stop adding rules
levels.goal: Your entry model isn’t a collection.

debrief.saw: Three checklists, each tempting you to add or swap a rule.
debrief.know: The Dayli ICC sequence decides entries. FVGs never add, remove or replace a step.
debrief.unknown: Nothing. This is about keeping the method clean.

steps.text: Bullish structure. Displacement up left a bullish FVG. Price is pulling back toward it.

lens.context: Displaced delivery left a bullish FVG. Price may revisit it.

options.label: WAIT
options.why: Disciplined read. Context is supportive. The entry sequence isn’t complete.

options.label: ENTER LONG at the FVG
options.feedback: The FVG doesn’t replace the sequence.

debrief.saw: Bullish structure, a displaced move up, a bullish FVG, and price pulling back.
debrief.know: The context is supportive. The Dayli ICC sequence is incomplete.
debrief.unknown: Whether the sequence forms. Until it does: WAIT.
debrief.good: ✓ DISCIPLINED READ. Context noted. No entry without the sequence.

questionBank.question: Two moves start and end at the same prices. One crawls with overlap, one moves in three big candles. What’s different?
Which question does this section add to your chart reading?
questionBank.why: Don’t just ask where price went. Ask how it got there.

questionBank.question: Price prints three large candles in one direction with little overlap. Best description?
options: Displacement: strong, one-sided delivery in that moment
questionBank.why: Momentum is information. Not a complete trade plan.

questionBank.question: Your friend says, “That candle displaced. I’m buying.” What’s missing?
options: Structure, the entry sequence and a plan for being wrong
questionBank.why: Displacement alone isn’t a trade plan.

questionBank.question: What best describes imbalance?
options: Price moved with little two-sided trading
A zone price must return to

questionBank.question: Imbalance vs FVG: which is true?
options: An FVG is one specific three-candle measurement of imbalance
Imbalance is a type of FVG

questionBank.question: What defines a bullish FVG?
options: The gap between candle 1’s high and candle 3’s low
The space between two swing highs

questionBank.question: What defines a bearish FVG?
options: The gap between candle 1’s low and candle 3’s high
questionBank.why: The mirror of a bullish FVG.

questionBank.question: You spot a bullish FVG. It is automatically…
options: None of these: not support, not a target, not an entry
questionBank.why: Before your brain turns it into an entry rule 😂

questionBank.question: Is an imbalanced-looking move better than a balanced-looking move?
questionBank.why: Different delivery. Not good or bad.

questionBank.question: Bearish external structure. A strong bullish displacement happens but stays below the relevant lower high. Did structure change?
options: No, the relevant lower high is intact

questionBank.question: Does price have to fill every FVG?
options: No. It may revisit quickly, later, or never

questionBank.question: An FVG filled last time. What does that tell you about the next one?
options: Nothing guaranteed. Each one is its own story

questionBank.question: Which FVG is most likely relevant?
options: One formed in the displacement that broke structure, near current price
The biggest one on the chart
questionBank.why: The existence of a concept is not the same as relevance.

questionBank.question: Your chart has nine FVG boxes and you can’t see the structure. What now?
options: Delete what doesn’t help you read the structure
questionBank.why: If the drawing makes you forget the structure, it’s hurting you.

questionBank.question: A valid Dayli ICC sequence formed, but there’s no FVG. What does that mean?
options: Wait for an FVG fill first
questionBank.why: We don’t force our method to fit another concept.
